learningObjective: Distinguish the compute and memory characteristics of prefill and decode phases in autoregressive LLM inference.

canonicalClaims.claim: In batch-1 LLM inference, prefill is compute-bound on the QKV/MLP GEMMs (intensity scales with prompt length P), while decode is memory-bandwidth bound (each linear op is a batch-1 GEMV with intensity ~1 flop/byte).
nonImplications: Does not imply the classification holds at large batch size for decode.
Does not imply prefill is always faster per user; wall-clock depends on P.

misconceptions.claim: Prefill and decode have the same arithmetic intensity because they use the same weights.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Intensity depends on activation shape reuse; P tokens reuse weights P times.

misconceptions.claim: Decode is compute-bound; that's why it needs quantization.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Decode is bandwidth-bound; quantization helps precisely because it reduces bandwidth.

misconceptions.claim: Prefill is memory-bound because it reads all weights once.
misconceptions.whyWrong: For non-trivial P, GEMMs have compute-bound intensity; weights are streamed but many flops per byte are extracted.

implementationFacts: vLLM, SGLang, and TRT-LLM all track prefill vs decode as distinct scheduling classes.
Chunked prefill and continuous batching are motivated by this asymmetry.
performanceScenarios: Large batches turn decode into an aggregated GEMV that can approach compute-bound (batched matmul).
